absent: Complete entry behavior and earlier capability cases for the virtual CPU fault capability handler beyond the notified tail fragment.

Native implementations behind delegated helpers for MSR filter, performance filter, timer, interrupt controller, routing, clock, TSC, pvclock, Xen shared info, guest mapping, event file and port limit operations.
Full layouts of virtual machine, architecture state, virtual CPU, clock data, Xen attribute union, port descriptor and timer structures beyond fields touched in fragments.

Numeric values and bit definitions for capability identifiers, ioctl commands except the compatibility MSR filter number, clock flags, Xen attribute types, event channel types and error mappings beyond observed returns.
Behavior when optional interrupt controller, Xen and HyperV builds are disabled and when backend encryption hooks are absent beyond returning unsupported.
Exact semantics of master clock versus base counter selection, TSC page refresh and guest time update pairing beyond offset derivation described.
Whether listed stubs for CPU topology query and one time warning are exercised by in scope code, as no use was visible in routed fragments.

findings.text: Architecture VM and VCPU ioctl handlers plus power management and compatibility handlers are exposed for generic dispatch.
Compatibility VM ioctl entry accepts only the MSR filter compatibility command and reports other commands with ENOTTY, with user copy failure reported as EFAULT.
Compatibility MSR range descriptor carries four 32 bit fields for flags, count, base and truncated user bitmap address.
Compatibility MSR filter carries a 32 bit flag word followed by a fixed array of range descriptors sized by the architectural maximum.
MSR filter compatibility command is a write direction KVMIO ioctl numbered 0xc6 sized for the compatibility filter structure.

Compatibility filter installation copies the compatibility structure from user space, preserves flags counts and bases while widening each truncated bitmap address to a native pointer, then delegates to the native installer.
Architecture power management entry maps hibernation prepare and suspend prepare to guest pause handling and completes other phases without action, always returning NOTIFY_DONE.
Suspend handling attempts to mark every virtual CPU of the machine as paused for clock purposes and reports success regardless of per CPU outcome.
VCPU ioctl entry supports only the memory encryption operation when a backend handler exists, otherwise reporting ENOIOCTLCMD.
VM ioctl entry multiplexes timing, clock, interrupt controller, timer, boot identifier, Xen, HyperV, encryption and filtering operations and reports unknown commands with ENOTTY.
Notification configuration splits a 64 bit argument into high half for window and low half for exit flags and stores both under the machine lock.

Huge page NX disable requires reboot privilege in the root namespace, a zero argument and zero created CPUs, setting a persistent flag under lock on success and failing with EPERM or EINVAL otherwise.

APIC bus period configuration rejects zero and values overflowing a 32 bit maximum scaled by 128, requires an in kernel interrupt chip and zero created CPUs, storing the period under lock and failing with EINVAL or ENXIO otherwise.

Huge page NX disable is treated as host wide risk because a guest could crash the system through a processor erratum, so container scope is explicitly not accepted and root namespace privilege is required.
APIC period validation guards a downstream timer to time conversion against arithmetic overflow using the largest programmable divider.
The machine lock serializes notification state, huge page policy, APIC period, identity mapping, interrupt chip mode and timer pointer, boot identifier and default TSC frequency.

Clock retrieval returns the paravirtual clock snapshot to user space with EFAULT on copy failure, while clock installation validates flag bits with EINVAL, refreshes hypervisor timing under an update window, avoids backward steps for real time, and derives the offset from master time when enabled else from the base counter.

Identity mapping, boot identifier and default TSC frequency are changeable only before any CPU exists, with boot identifier bounded by global and per VM maxima failing with EBUSY or EINVAL, and zero TSC frequency selecting host frequency while controlled platforms reject values at or above the guest maximum.

In kernel interrupt chip creation transitions from absent to present only without an existing chip, without protected end of interrupt and without created CPUs, progressing through PIC setup then IOAPIC setup then default routing with cleanup on failure before publishing kernel mode with ordering and clearing the absent inhibition.

Timer creation fails with EEXIST if a timer exists and with ENOENT without an in kernel PIC, with one variant supplying default speaker behavior and the other copying configuration from user space, and all timer state access requires an existing timer else ENXIO.
Interrupt chip state access requires a fully present in kernel chip else ENXIO and operates on a kernel copy, with retrieval copying the result back and reporting EFAULT on user copy failure.

Memory encryption VM and VCPU operations are available only when backend hooks exist else ENOTTY, with region operations copying a descriptor from user space before delegation and reporting EFAULT on copy failure.
Xen attribute setters and getters are exposed for VM ioctl dispatch to configure and query compatibility state.

Xen attribute installation supports long mode, shared info by guest frame or host address, upcall vector, event channel, version and runstate flag, rejecting long mode enable on 32 bit hosts, misaligned host addresses, non zero vectors below 0x10 and runstate without scheduler accounting, and re initializing shared state when an active mapping changes.

Xen attribute retrieval reports stored mode, vector, version and runstate values, reports shared info as invalid guest frame or zero host address when inactive, is unavailable for runstate without scheduler accounting with EOPNOTSUPP, and reports unknown types with ENOENT.

The Xen subsystem lock protects mode, shared info cache, upcall vector, version, runstate flag and the port table, with a sleepable read section covering shared info activation and a grace period separating removal from release.

Xen event channel ports move through assign for creation, update for priority and destination changes, deassign for single removal and reset for bulk removal, with reset collecting entries before waiting for readers then releasing each object.

Event channel dispatch treats reset as global, validates ports as non zero and below the maximum, routes deassign update and empty flags to removal modification and creation respectively, and rejects other flags with EINVAL.

Event channel assignment accepts only processor local and interdomain types, requires local delivery to loop to its own port, allows interdomain delivery as a valid guest port with two level priority or as an event file, and reports duplicate ports with EEXIST and allocation failures with ENOMEM.

Event channel update requires an existing port of matching type with unchanged non zero delivery port and two level priority, allowing only priority refresh and destination CPU change with cache invalidation, failing with ENOENT or EINVAL otherwise.

User copy failures surface as EFAULT, port table exhaustion is translated to already exists, and event file release plus object freeing are deferred until after a read grace period to avoid use after removal.
